Run 283 shows the 400 tuning stays are contiguous (2020000000–2020000399). It gave me sel2 (100 stays, no overlap with sel1) and two more chunks, C3 and C4, for the factual check. The dose_edit CSV has per stay-hour rows (stay_id, hour, edit, shift, shift_se, factual, reached). The target helpers `true_shift_ins(sid, hour, factor, beta_)` and `true_shift_ne(sid, hour, factor, gam_)` work on the tuning panels, so targets can be computed for any tuning stays.

Next is the out-of-sample check of the calibration: the dose_edit with the current edit (E5) on sel2. I'll then compute the record-based targets on sel2's reached stay-hours.

Insulin is right if its readouts land within about 10% of the sel2 targets (as on sel1). The NE readouts should keep the same pattern: x1/2 close, x2 about 30% of target. A large insulin miss on sel2 would mean the sel1 calibration overfitted Monte Carlo noise or that sel1's stays were unusual.
